record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Determine an intrinsic characterisation for the class H of functions h analytic in D that admit a decomposition of the form 2h = f + f −1 for some function f in the class S of normalised univalent functions in D. (Here f −1 denotes the function inverse to f and it is assumed that f −1 has an analytic continuation to D.) Notice that the functions z 7→ z and z 7→ z/(1 − z 2 ) both belong to H. In particular, does the function z 7→ z + a sin(2πz) belong to H for any non-zero constant a? (F. Holland)

evidence.quote: Determine an intrinsic characterisation for the class H of functions h analytic in D that admit a decomposition of the form 2h = f + f −1 for some function f in the class S of normalised univalent functions in D.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and let $S$ denote the class of normalised univalent functions on $\mathbb{D}$, i.e. functions $f$ that are holomorphic and injective on $\mathbb{D}$ with $f(0)=0$ and $f'(0)=1$. Let $H$ denote the class of functions $h$ holomorphic on $\mathbb{D}$ for which there exists $f\in S$ such that the inverse function $f^{-1}$ admits a holomorphic continuation to all of $\mathbb{D}$ and
$$2h(z) = f(z) + f^{-1}(z) \qquad (z\in\mathbb{D}).$$

(a) Find an intrinsic characterisation of the class $H$, that is, a description of the members of $H$ stated purely in terms of properties of the function $h$ on $\mathbb{D}$ (without reference to the auxiliary function $f$).

(b) Note that $h(z)=z$ (taking $f(z)=z$) and $h(z)=z/(1-z^2)$ (taking $f(z)=z/(1-z)$) belong to $H$. Determine whether the function
$$h(z) = z + a\sin(2\pi z)$$
belongs to $H$ for any non-zero constant $a\in\mathbb{C}$.
